plays.story: Chainalysis and Register both dig into how North Korea's fake job interview playbook enabled the $6.3B Binance heist, with a compromised AI tool as the entry point.

angles.itsalreadypriced: Title: 'Binance's $6.3B Nightmare: Inside the Hack That Grayscale Calls a Temporary Setback' — track the market fallout, the 81% of stolen Solana now routed through THORChain, and whether 'crypto shrugs it off' narrative holds up.
angles.itsalreadywhen: Title: 'The Job Interview That Cost $6.3 Billion: North Korea's Fake-Recruiter Playbook, Decoded' — use Chainalysis's research on DPRK's 'dozens of attacks before Binance' to warn security teams about hiring-pipeline social engineering and compromised AI tooling as attack vectors.

plays.story: Post-hack fallout: Dark Reading examines the single compromised laptop that enabled the Binance breach, while Coinbase publicly flexes its cold-storage posture in response.

angles.itsalreadypriced: Title: 'Coinbase's Not-So-Subtle Shade: 99% Cold Storage After Binance's $6.3B Mess' — frame as a competitive security flex and what it signals for exchange trust post-hack.
angles.itsalreadywhen: Title: 'One Compromised Laptop, Billions Lost: The Attack-Path Test Every CISO Should Run This Week' — turn the Binance postmortem into a practical attack-path audit checklist for any org, not just exchanges.

plays.story: Mercado Bitcoin's hack containment failed — the attack continued hours after the exchange claimed it was contained, and Chainalysis helped freeze ~$10M in stolen funds.

angles.itsalreadypriced: Title: 'Mercado Bitcoin's Reopening Gamble: Can a Promise to Cover Losses Rebuild Trust?' — cover the phased reopening and what it means for users and the exchange's credibility.
angles.itsalreadywhen: Title: 'The Hack Wasn't Over When They Said It Was: What Mercado Bitcoin's Containment Failure Teaches About Incident Response' — dissect the gap between declared containment and actual attacker persistence, tying in Chainalysis's freeze operation as a rare win.

plays.story: EN World's first impressions of the Dungeons & Dragons x World of Warcraft tabletop crossover, paired with the ongoing WoW Deep Dive race-lore series (Draenei, Dracthyr).

angles.bizzal-games: Title: 'First Impressions: Is D&D's World of Warcraft Crossover Worth Clearing Your Table's Schedule For?' — a hands-on breakdown of the new ruleset for GMs deciding whether to run it.
angles.itsalreadywritten: Title: 'Writing Azeroth at Your Table: What the D&D x WoW Crossover Gets Right (and Wrong) About Adapting Game Lore' — use the Draenei/Dracthyr deep dives to explore how MMO backstory translates (or doesn't) into tabletop narrative design.
